text:
Fixed and verified.

RED first, with an unusually clear failure message: the new cancel-side test observed
  InvocationFailed(SpawnFailed(Unknown, Diagnostics(... ssh-transport-disconnected, TransportDisconnected(true, response channel closed, None) ...)))
The adapter had the afterRequestWrite = true flag in its hands and threw it away, reporting a safely repeatable invocation failure for a scancel that may already have run.

Fix: ssh/Slurm.scala cancel now mirrors the submit path at :54, matching AgentFailure.TransportDisconnected(true, _, _) and returning CancellationAttempt.Completed(CancellationResult.Unknown(...)) with diagnostic code cancellation-acknowledgement-unknown — the same code the CLI backend already produces on timeout (SlurmCliScheduler.scala:226), so the two backends now agree. Disconnect BEFORE the write still yields a typed invocation failure, which is correct and is covered by a second test.

Also corrected the class doc at :39-43, which stated the submit law only and read as though cancellation had no such rule.

Verification: 2 new tests in ssh/RemoteSchedulerSuite (the bead noted no cancel-side test existed). Full suite 319, 0 failed. scalafmt clean.

Scope note: this fixes the LAW. It does not fix the flattening — every AgentFailure variant still collapses to SpawnFailed(Unknown) through invocationFailure at :219, so a ProtocolViolation on a zero-exit ssh is still reported as a definite "not submitted" when AcceptanceUncertainty.ResponseUnparseable exists for exactly that case. That is P8.D5 and remains open.
